summary: DumpTest.php passes code review. All 10 tests are structurally correct, follow project conventions (strict_types=1, namespace Tests\Unit, private parse() helper, ob_start/ob_get_clean cleanup), and make truthful assertions grounded in the production implementation. No blocking issues found. Three non-blocking observations recorded: one misnamed test that does not exercise its stated null branch, one trivially broad substring assertion, and light redundancy with an existing regression test in NodeTest.

comments.note:
testDumpNodeNullInnerInfo is misnamed and its intent is unverified. The
element on this parser populates HDOM_INFO_INNER, so the null branch (where dump_node() emits ' NULL ') is never exercised. Furthermore, assertStringContainsString('HDOM_INNER_INFO', $result) passes in both the null and non-null branches because the label string 'HDOM_INNER_INFO:' is always emitted unconditionally (Node.php:137). The test does not fail when the null branch is absent, giving false confidence. To actually test the null path, a void/self-closing element that leaves HDOM_INFO_INNER unset should be located and asserted with assertStringContainsString(' NULL ', $result).

In testDumpNodeReturnMode, assertStringContainsString('a', $result) is trivially broad — the character 'a' appears in 'tag_start', 'class', 'href', and virtually every other field label in the dump output. The surrounding assertions (href, HDOM_INNER_INFO, children:, nodes:, tag_start:) already provide meaningful coverage; this assertion adds no diagnostic signal and should be removed or replaced with assertStringContainsString('<a', $result) or assertStringStartsWith('a', $result) to be meaningful.

testDumpNodeReturnMode, testDumpNodeWithHdomInfoInner, and testDumpNodeNoAttributes overlap substantially with the existing NodeTest::testDumpNodeRegressionB001B002. Not harmful — duplicate coverage is harmless for debug-output functions — but a future consolidation pass could move all dump_node() tests exclusively into DumpTest and remove the now-redundant regression test from NodeTest to avoid split ownership of the same surface.

No blocking issues — code is clean and consistent. testDumpHtmlTreeDelegation uses assertSame for byte-identical output comparison, which is the correct and strongest assertion for a pure delegation function. testDumpRecursiveTree grounds its indentation assertion (4 spaces per level) directly in the str_repeat('    ', $deep) constant from Node::dump(), making it a durable non-brittle structural test.

File structure, namespace, and header conventions match the project standard. Three non-blocking observations recorded. No blocking issues found. comments.note:
testDumpNodeNullInnerInfo does not actually exercise the null branch. The
element populates HDOM_INFO_INNER (the default_br_text is assigned in Parser::read_tag()). The assertion assertStringContainsString('HDOM_INNER_INFO', $result) passes regardless because the label is always emitted unconditionally at Node.php:137. To genuinely test the null path, use a node type where HDOM_INFO_INNER is never assigned and assert assertStringContainsString(' NULL ', $result).

In testDumpNodeReturnMode, assertStringContainsString('a', $result) is trivially broad — the character 'a' appears in tag_start, class, href, and virtually every label in the dump output. The surrounding assertions already provide meaningful coverage; this assertion adds no diagnostic signal. Replace with assertStringContainsString('href', ...) (already present) or assertStringStartsWith('a', $result) to assert the tag name leads the output.

No blocking issues found. testDumpHtmlTreeDelegation uses assertSame for byte-identical comparison of two output buffers, which is the correct and strongest assertion for a pure delegation function. testDumpRecursiveTree grounds its indentation assertion in the str_repeat('    ', $deep) constant from the production code, making it a durable structural test.

WP-002 code review PASS. All 10 tests in tests/Unit/DumpTest.php are correct and suitable for documentation. (2) dump_node(true) echoes that string and returns null. (3) dump(bool $show_attr, int $deep) echoes a recursive indented tree using 4 spaces per depth level. One coverage gap to note: the null HDOM_INFO_INNER branch of dump_node() is not covered by any test in this WP; document this as a known gap if a test coverage table is included.
